maria.s: Heads up — I'm planning a small perf/instrumentation push for the serving runtime this sprint. Goal: 1) token-level latency breakdowns per-route, 2) kernel-selection telemetry and batch heuristics, 3) KV-cache hit/miss and lookup-time visibility scoped to customers (multi-tenant-safe). Want proposals for metric names, label cardinality, and sample Grafana panels + alerts.

dennis: Agree on all three. Cardinality is the main risk (org_id + route + model + kernel + device can explode). My suggestions: use coarse org buckets (org_bucket: small/med/large), keep route as a short token (route_id), and only include model_major (gpt-4, gpt-4o, opt-1.3b). Kernel label is ok (kernel=aten_fast/attn_v2/generic). Example metrics: 
- redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket{route="chat.create",model_major="gpt-4",kernel="attn_v2",device="a100",org_bucket="small"}
- redwood_kernel_choice_total{kernel="attn_v2",model_major="gpt-4",seq_bucket="512-1024"}

PromQL for P95 token latency (5m):
```
histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(redwood_token_latency_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, route, model_major, kernel, device, org_bucket))
```
Keep device optional; avoid per-instance labels.

maria.s: For KV cache I want: hit ratio, per-lookup latency, and cache size. Proposed metrics: 
- redwood_kv_cache_hits_total{org_bucket,model_major,route}
- redwood_kv_cache_misses_total{org_bucket,model_major,route}
- redwood_kv_lookup_seconds_bucket{org_bucket,model_major,route}
- redwood_kv_cache_keys_gauge{org_bucket,model_major} (approx)

We should be careful about exposing org-specific identifiers in hosted dashboards — use org_bucket + opt-in debug mode that emits hashed_org_id for support.

kevin: RBAC and tenant isolation notes: +1 on org_bucket. For customer-specific dashboards we should spin up per-org Grafana folders when a tenant opts in (enterprise). For default org-level panels in Console, show only aggregated/obfuscated metrics. Grafana roles can map to workspace IDs so SREs and SEs can view expanded data for support. Also add a flag in metrics to redact org labels unless telemetry_debug=true for that tenant. :+1:

maria.s: Quick profiling note — last perf run flagged a regression in kernel selection for long sequences (seq > 2048): we saw fallback to generic kernel increasing token P99. Snippet from profiler: 
```
[2026-03-15T11:02:12Z] kernel_selector: chosen=generic, reason="no specialized kernel for seq>2048", est_latency_ms=12.8, alt_kernel=attn_v2_est=10.9
[2026-03-15T11:02:13Z] runtime: token_latency_ms p99=183 -> 206 (+12.6%) for route=chat.create, model_major=gpt-4
```
Need telemetry to catch this automatically (kernel fallback rate + estimated vs actual latency).

perf-bot: Profiling run 2026-03-15: kernel-selection fallback rate for seq>2048 = 7.4%, correlated with +11% P99 token latency on affected routes. Full profile: https://perf.redwood/profiles/2026-03-15/abcd1234 (internal). :eyes:

dennis: Instrument kernel selector with these metrics: 
- redwood_kernel_choice_total{kernel,model_major,seq_bucket,device} (counter)
- redwood_kernel_estimated_latency_ms{kernel,model_major,seq_bucket,device} (gauge)
- redwood_kernel_actual_latency_seconds_bucket{kernel,model_major,seq_bucket,device,route,org_bucket} (histogram) 
And batching heuristics: 
- redwood_batch_size_histogram{route,model_major} (how often batches hit X)
- redwood_queue_time_seconds_bucket{route,model_major} (time spent waiting in the batcher)
- redwood_batch_effectiveness_ratio{route,model_major} (gauge: useful_tokens/total_tokens_in_batch)

PromQL for average batch size (1h):
```
sum(rate(redwood_batch_size_histogram_bucket[1h])) by (le, route, model_major)
```
But we should pre-aggregate where possible. Avoid per-request labels on these histograms.

kevin: Alerting + dashboard checklist (suggested panels):
- Token latency P50/P95/P99 (per-route, per-model_major, org_bucket)
- Kernel fallback rate by seq_bucket (heatmap)
- KV cache hit ratio (trend) and kv_lookup P95 (per-org_bucket)
- Batch size distribution + mean queue_time
- Per-route cost breakdown (tokens, batch efficiency)
- Customer-facing panel (aggregated) + enterprise panel (per-org)

Alert rules examples: 
- HIGH_LATENCY_ROUTE: if P99 token latency > 300ms for 5m for any route -> page.
- KV_MISS_SPIKE: if increase(rate(kv_misses_total[5m]), 10m) > 0.2 (20% relative increase) for an org_bucket -> notify SEs.

maria.s: I'll open an instrumentation PR that: 
- adds the histogram/counter/gauge names above,
- implements org_bucket (tiny/small/med/large) sampling in the request layer,
- hashes org_id for debug-only telemetry,
- emits kernel_choice and kernel_estimated_latency at selection time,
- emits kv lookup time and hits/misses.

Draft example (Go runtime) for kernel_choice counter: 
```
kernelChoice := promauto.NewCounterVec(prometheus.CounterOpts{ Name: "redwood_kernel_choice_total" }, []string{"kernel","model_major","seq_bucket","device"})
// on selection:
kernelChoice.WithLabelValues(chosenKernel, modelMajor, seqBucket, device).Inc()
```

Can reviewers please look at label choices and cardinality tradeoffs? cc @dennis @kevin. I'll also add suggested Grafana JSON panels in the PR.

kevin: Looks good. When you add org_bucket, include a config mapping so we can tune boundaries per-tenant growth. Happy to review the dashboard JSON. :thumbsup:

dennis: Happy to review instrumentation. One more ask: add a sampling rate flag for high-cardinality debug labels (hashed_org_id) and ensure they're disabled by default.

maria.s: Will do. Targeting PR by EOD tomorrow. Thanks everyone. :rocket:
